# System One, accuracy-first

*The same decision layer as [Build a System One](tutorial.html), rebuilt
for the other side of the trade: pay time for quality. Two teachers on
your LAN instead of one, a judge that generalises from what it learned
instead of counting features, and a learning rule that never writes a
label the two teachers dispute. Every program on this page is complete,
every output was produced by running it. Nothing leaves your network.*

> **Too long, want the code?** The complete project is on GitHub:
> [tutorials/system-one-accurate](https://github.com/FabianoDicheti/maned-lang-docs/tree/main/tutorials/system-one-accurate) —
> the programs, the shell runbook and the Python app, with a README of the
> commands from two fresh workers to a running loop. The speed-first
> edition, with its Kotlin and Rust apps, is
> [system-one-tutorial](https://github.com/FabianoDicheti/maned-lang-docs/tree/main/tutorials/system-one-tutorial).

## Two editions of one loop

The first tutorial built a System One that answers a classification
question in milliseconds from its own memory and asks an XLM-RoBERTa
worker when it cannot. We then measured it on nine public datasets, 240
texts learned per dataset, 33 unseen texts each, and learned three things:

- **The count judge does not generalise.** On texts it has never seen it
  scores 0.35 with 40 texts learned and 0.40 with 240: the memory grows,
  the judge does not. It is excellent at what it was built for, answering
  a text it has seen before in 8 ms, and nothing else.
- **A second teacher is worth more than a second description.** An
  entailment model (mDeBERTa-v3, served by the same bare-metal platform
  as the XLM) is right on 50 % of unseen texts against the XLM's 47 %, and
  when the two **agree** they are right 75 % of the time. On this corpus
  the agreement is a far better filter for what to learn than any
  confidence threshold of either teacher alone.
- **A judge over the embedding grows with volume.** A centroid per label,
  the mean of the whitened XLM vectors of the texts learned under it, goes
  from 0.39–0.42 to 0.44 between 40 and 240 texts learned in the live loop
  (0.48 offline with every teacher label, 0.59 when the labels are the
  truth). It answers a quarter to a half of unseen texts at the second
  teacher's accuracy, without calling it.

So there are two sensible systems, not one compromise. The
**speed-first** edition pays for nothing it does not need: one worker, a
count judge, an answer in milliseconds when the memory knows the text, a
400 ms XLM call when it does not. The **accuracy-first** edition on this
page spends a second worker, one embedding per unseen text and a second
memory to be right more often and to learn only what it can trust.

| | speed-first | accuracy-first |
|---|---|---|
| known text | the count memory, ~8 ms | the same |
| unseen text | the count judge's tier, else the XLM's zero-shot label (~0.4 s) | one XLM embedding → the **prototype judge**; when it is not sure, the **NLI worker** decides (~0.25 s per candidate on bare metal) |
| what is learned | the XLM's label when its margin clears 70 ‰ | the NLI label when the XLM's zero-shot verdict agrees and the NLI margin clears 250 ‰; everything else waits for you in `pending.tsv` |
| memories | `memory.dqt` | `memory.dqt` + `protos.dqt`, one centroid per label |
| apps | Python, Kotlin, Rust | Python |

Everything that is not on this page — the worker stick, the model, the
count memory, the lookup program, the record, the service — is the first
tutorial's, unchanged: the project folder carries the same files. The five
parts below are what changed.

## 1. The second worker

*An entailment model on the same bare-metal platform as the XLM: a
question per candidate label — does this text entail this sentence? — and
three logits back. The hypotheses are written like the descriptions were.*

### 1. What it is

`maned-nli-bark` is the same kernel family as the XLM worker of the first
tutorial with a different model inside: **mDeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-xnli**,
a multilingual natural-language-inference model as exact integers. Its
one request is `POST /api/nli` with the token ids of a pair *(premise,
hypothesis)*, and the reply is three logits — entailment, neutral,
contradiction — plus the sha256 of the reply and of the model that served
it. Like the XLM worker it is deterministic to the byte on every machine.

Zero-shot classification with it is Hugging Face's rule: one hypothesis
per candidate label, the softmax over the entailment logits, the largest
wins. Each candidate costs one forward pass, about 230 ms on the Ryzen
worker of our bench, so a three-label question costs about 0.7 s and a
fourteen-label one about 3 s. That is the price of this edition, and
the prototype judge of part 2 exists to pay it as rarely as possible.

Boot a second computer from the stick, provision the NLI model onto its
disk as part 2 of the first tutorial did with the XLM, and put its address
in a second env file. Its login is its own:

```sh
umask 077
cat > ~/.config/maned/nli.env <<'EOF'
export S1_NLI_HOST=192.0.2.11
export NLI_USER=worker
export NLI_PASS=12345
EOF
```

`/api/status` says `service: maned-nli-bark` when it is the right one.

### 2. Hypotheses beside descriptions

The XLM lane describes a label; the NLI lane tests a sentence about the
text. The two are not the same sentence: a description is written to be
*near* the texts of its label in embedding space, a hypothesis is written
to be *true of* them. `corpus/hypotheses.tsv` has one per label:

```text
urgent	This message is urgent and needs action right now.
later	This message is low priority and can wait.
careful	This message contains legal or financial terms that must be read carefully.
```

The registry mirrors the descriptions': `work/descs_nli.tsv` holds
`name<TAB>hypothesis`, one row per label, nothing embedded. When a label
has no hypothesis on file, its description is used as one — it works,
less well.

### 3. The tokenizer runs on your side

`00_download.sh` fetches one more file: the NLI model's SentencePiece
model, 4 MB, MIT. The pair is tokenized like `DebertaV2Tokenizer` does —
`[CLS] text [SEP] hypothesis [SEP]`, ids used raw, the longer side cut
first past 512 pieces — by `nli/nli_lane.py`, which is the whole client:
login, one request per candidate hypothesis, the reply's hashes checked,
retries on a busy worker, and a reply cache you can switch on for a
benchmark. It writes the entailment logits as one csv row for the program
of part 2.

```sh
. ~/.config/maned/xlm.env; . ~/.config/maned/nli.env
./00_download.sh
```

```text
work/sentencepiece.bpe.model: kept
work/xlm-stats.dqt: kept
work/nli-spm.model: kept
work/xlmr-large.int32.dqt: skipped (WITH_WEIGHTS=1 fetches it; only 00_provision.mnd needs it)
download done
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""nli_lane.py - the entailment worker call of the accuracy edition.

For every candidate hypothesis row of work/descs_nli.tsv (the rows
work/q/cand_d.csv marks 1), POST the pair (work/q/text.txt, hypothesis) to the
NLI worker (maned-nli-bark, mDeBERTa-v3 as int32: POST /api/nli -> the three
logits entailment / neutral / contradiction) and write

  work/q/nli_e.csv    one row: the ENTAILMENT logit per hypothesis row
                      (decimal, 6 places; 0 for non-candidates) - the input
                      of 02_nli_classify.mnd
  work/q/nli_raw.json every reply (logits, clamps, tokens), for a trace

The pair is tokenized like DebertaV2Tokenizer does: the checkpoint's
SentencePiece model (work/nli-spm.model, 00_download.sh) with its ids used
raw, [CLS] text [SEP] hypothesis [SEP], truncated to 512 ids by cutting the
longer side first.

Env: S1_NLI_HOST (else the lines of $S1_NLI_ENV, default ~/.config/maned/nli.env,
else S1_WORKER_HOST), NLI_USER / NLI_PASS (else that file's, else XLM_USER /
XLM_PASS), NLI_PORT (4780), NLI_TIMEOUT (20 s), S1_NLI_CACHE (a jsonl reply
cache: the worker is deterministic, so a pair asked before is answered from the
file), NLI_MODEL_SHA (else nli/model_nli.sha256: the model the worker must serve).
Exit non-zero on any worker error, so the shell stops.
Standard library only, plus the `sentencepiece` package.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import struct
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__))
PAD, CLS, SEP, UNK = 0, 1, 2, 3
MAX_TOKENS = 512


class PairTokenizer:
    def __init__(self, model_file):
        import sentencepiece as spm
        self.sp = spm.SentencePieceProcessor(model_file=model_file)
        assert self.sp.id_to_piece(CLS) == "[CLS]" and self.sp.id_to_piece(SEP) == "[SEP]", "not a DeBERTa-v3 spm.model"

    def encode_pair(self, premise, hypothesis):
        a, b = [int(i) for i in self.sp.encode(premise)], [int(i) for i in self.sp.encode(hypothesis)]
        over = len(a) + len(b) + 3 - MAX_TOKENS
        while over > 0:  # longest_first: drop from the longer sequence's end
            if len(a) >= len(b):
                a.pop()
            else:
                b.pop()
            over -= 1
        return [CLS] + a + [SEP] + b + [SEP]


class Worker:
    """the worker's HTTP API: /api/auth for a token, /api/nli for the logits"""

    def __init__(self, host, port, user, password, timeout=20):
        self.base = "http://%s:%d" % (host, port)
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.user, self.password = user, password
        self.token = None

    def _req(self, method, path, body=None, auth=True):
        data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=data, method=method)
        if data is not None:
            req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        if auth and self.token:
            req.add_header("X-Caramel-Token", self.token)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout) as r:
                return r.status, json.loads(r.read() or b"{}")
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            try:
                return e.code, json.loads(e.read() or b"{}")
            except ValueError:
                return e.code, {}

    def login(self):
        code, j = self._req("POST", "/api/auth", {"username": self.user, "password": self.password}, auth=False)
        if code != 200 or "token" not in j:
            raise SystemExit("nli_lane: login failed (HTTP %s: %s)" % (code, j))
        self.token = j["token"]

    def nli(self, ids, model_sha=None):
        """-> (http code, reply); the reply's logits must hash to its sha256, and come from the expected model"""
        if self.token is None:
            self.login()
        code, j = self._req("POST", "/api/nli", {"ids": ids})
        if code == 401:  # the session token expired (long runs): log in again once
            self.login()
            code, j = self._req("POST", "/api/nli", {"ids": ids})
        if code == 200:
            z = j.get("logits", [])
            got = hashlib.sha256(struct.pack("<%di" % len(z), *z)).hexdigest()
            if len(z) != 3 or got != j.get("sha256"):
                raise SystemExit("nli_lane: reply corrupt - logits do not hash to their sha256: refused")
            if model_sha and not model_sha.startswith(j.get("model_sha256", "?")):
                raise SystemExit("nli_lane: the worker serves model %s, expected %s" % (j.get("model_sha256"), model_sha[:12]))
        return code, j


def call_with_retry(w, ids, sha, tries=6):
    """the platform serves one request at a time and a LAN drops the odd connection:
    a BUSY/5xx reply or a socket error is retried with backoff and logged to
    work/q/nli_lane.err; only a persistent failure stops the run"""
    last = None
    for k in range(tries):
        try:
            code, j = w.nli(ids, model_sha=sha)
            if code == 200:
                return code, j
            last = "HTTP %s: %s" % (code, j)
        except SystemExit:
            raise
        except Exception as e:  # URLError, timeout, a reset connection
            last = repr(e)
            w.token = None
        with open("work/q/nli_lane.err", "a") as f:
            f.write("%s try %d: %s\n" % (time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), k + 1, last))
        time.sleep(0.5 * (k + 1))
    sys.exit("nli_lane: /api/nli failed %d times: %s" % (tries, last))


def nli_login():
    """the NLI worker's address and identity: the environment first, then
    ~/.config/maned/nli.env ($S1_NLI_ENV), then the XLM worker's own (one box, one login)"""
    kv = {}
    env = os.environ.get("S1_NLI_ENV", os.path.expanduser("~/.config/maned/nli.env"))
    if os.path.isfile(env):
        for line in open(env, encoding="utf-8"):
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith("export "):
                line = line[7:]
            if "=" in line and not line.startswith("#"):
                k, v = line.split("=", 1)
                kv[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip("'\"")
    host = os.environ.get("S1_NLI_HOST") or kv.get("S1_NLI_HOST") or os.environ.get("S1_WORKER_HOST")
    user = os.environ.get("NLI_USER") or kv.get("NLI_USER") or kv.get("XLM_USER") or os.environ.get("XLM_USER")
    pw = os.environ.get("NLI_PASS") or kv.get("NLI_PASS") or kv.get("XLM_PASS") or os.environ.get("XLM_PASS")
    if not (host and user and pw):
        sys.exit("nli_lane: set S1_NLI_HOST (and NLI_USER/NLI_PASS when its login differs) in the environment or %s" % env)
    return host, user, pw


def model_sha():
    s = os.environ.get("NLI_MODEL_SHA")
    if s is None:
        try:
            s = open(os.path.join(HERE, "model_nli.sha256")).read().strip()
        except OSError:
            s = ""
    return s or None


def main():
    host, user, pw = nli_login()
    w = Worker(host, int(os.environ.get("NLI_PORT", "4780")), user, pw, timeout=int(os.environ.get("NLI_TIMEOUT", "20")))
    spm_path = os.environ.get("NLI_SPM", "work/nli-spm.model")
    if not os.path.isfile(spm_path):
        sys.exit("nli_lane: %s is missing - run ./00_download.sh first" % spm_path)
    tok = PairTokenizer(spm_path)
    text = open("work/q/text.txt", encoding="utf-8").read().rstrip("\n")
    rows = [l.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1) for l in open("work/descs_nli.tsv", encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
    mask = [float(v) > 0 for v in open("work/q/cand_d.csv").read().strip().split(",")]
    assert len(mask) == len(rows), (len(mask), len(rows))
    sha = model_sha()
    cache_path = os.environ.get("S1_NLI_CACHE")
    cache = {}
    if cache_path and os.path.isfile(cache_path):
        for line in open(cache_path, encoding="utf-8"):
            if line.strip():
                c = json.loads(line)
                if sha is None or c.get("model_sha256") == sha:
                    cache[(c["text"], c["hypothesis"])] = c
    e, raw = [], []
    for (name, hyp), on in zip(rows, mask):
        if not on:
            e.append("0.000000")
            continue
        c = cache.get((text, hyp))
        if c is None:
            code, j = call_with_retry(w, tok.encode_pair(text, hyp), sha)
            z = [v / 10.0 ** j["scale"] for v in j["logits"]]
            c = {"text": text, "hypothesis": hyp, "model_sha256": j.get("model_sha256", sha), "tokens": j.get("tokens"), "logits": z, "clamps": j.get("clamps")}
            if cache_path:
                with open(cache_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    f.write(json.dumps(c, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        e.append("%.6f" % c["logits"][0])
        raw.append({"name": name, "hypothesis": hyp, "tokens": c["tokens"], "logits": c["logits"], "clamps": c["clamps"]})
    with open("work/q/nli_e.csv", "w") as f:
        f.write(",".join(e) + "\n")
    with open("work/q/nli_raw.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump({"text": text, "model_sha256": sha, "pairs": raw}, f)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Standard library plus `pip install sentencepiece`; the same package the
Python app of the first tutorial already needs for `manedpy`'s host-side
tokenizer.

## 2. The prototype judge

*One embedding of the text, two verdicts: the nearest label description,
as before, and the nearest learned centroid — a judge that gets better
with every text recorded under a label.*

### 1. A second memory

The count memory of the first tutorial is a `[4096, 32]` matrix of feature
counts: good at recognising a text it has seen, blind to one it has not.
The second memory is a `[32, 256]` matrix of vector sums: row *L* is the
sum of the whitened unit vectors of every text recorded under label *L*,
and `n[L]` how many. Its centroid is the row divided by `n`, normalised.
The two share `work/labels.tsv`: line *i* is column *i* of one and row *i*
of the other.

`00_init_protos.mnd`:

```mnd
# 00_init_protos.mnd -- the empty centroid memory of the accuracy edition
#
#   maned-run 00_init_protos.mnd       (once, after 00_init_memory.mnd; ./00_setup.sh does both)
#
# The second memory is ONE file with two tensors:
#
#   work/protos.dqt
#     sum  [32,256]  the sum of the whitened unit vectors (02_proto_classify.mnd's
#                    `u`, components at 10^-3) of every text recorded under each label
#     n    [1,32]    how many vectors each row sums
#
# Columns are the label slots of work/labels.tsv, shared with memory.dqt.
# 02_proto_classify.mnd turns a row into the label's centroid (its mean,
# warm-started with the label's anchor description, normalised) and scores an
# unseen text by cosine against every candidate's centroid; 03_record_proto.mnd
# adds one vector. Like the count memory, it is a pure function of the
# recorded texts: 06_rebuild.sh replays work/vectors.csv and gets the same bytes.
mnd::quantmax = 2147483;
mnd::quantmin = -2147483;
mnd::quantres = 3;

in::z = 32 256 zeros;
in::zn = 1 32 zeros;

calc::lambda_flow init(z, zn) {
    z 1 scalar_mul sum =
    zn 1 scalar_mul n =
} return sum, n;

out::sum = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "sum");
out::n = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "n");
```

```sh
./00_setup.sh
```

```text
work/memory.dqt and work/protos.dqt are empty; the memories start here
```

### 2. Anchors, then centroids

A label with no texts yet has a centroid of nothing. So each centroid is
warm-started with its **anchor**, the unit mean of the label's description
vectors — exactly the rows `02_label_embed.mnd` already produces — counted
as `warm` texts (3 in `proto_policy.csv`): the judge begins as the
zero-shot classifier of the first tutorial and becomes a nearest-centroid
classifier as texts arrive, with no switch and no second formula.

`02_proto_classify.mnd`:

```mnd
# 02_proto_classify.mnd -- the accuracy edition's judge: ONE embedding, two verdicts
#
#   (04_query.sh runs it for every text the known-text cache does not answer)
#
# The text is embedded on the XLM-R worker and whitened to the 256-d unit
# vector u exactly as in 02_xlm_classify.mnd. Then:
#
#   anchors    s = u . labs^T     the cosine to every label description (x10^6),
#              best = the nearest candidate description row - the zero-shot
#              verdict of the speed edition, unchanged
#   prototype  one centroid per label L from the centroid memory (protos.dqt):
#                c_L = unit( (warm * a_L + sum_L) / (warm + n_L) )
#              a_L the unit MEAN of L's description rows (its anchor), sum_L and
#              n_L the recorded vectors; `warm` (proto_policy.csv) is how many
#              texts the anchor is worth, so a label with no texts yet is judged
#              by its anchor alone and the anchor fades as real texts arrive.
#              ps = u . c^T (x10^6) over the candidates, pbest its argmax,
#              pmargin = best - second (x10^6), and the tier from the policy row
#              of the request's risk: 2 (auto) when pmargin >= t_auto AND the
#              winning label has learned at least min_n texts (an anchor-only
#              verdict is zero-shot, not memory: it never answers alone), 1 when
#              pmargin >= t_verify, else 0.
#
# The mean is taken BEFORE the norm: a sum of many unit vectors would overflow
# the int32 square inside isqrt after ~46 texts, a mean never does.
# u itself is written to work/q/u.csv so 03_record_proto.mnd can learn the
# text without asking the worker again.
#
# work/q/cand_d.csv is the [1,D] candidate mask over description rows and
# work/q/d2l.csv the [D,32] row->label one-hot, both written as 0.001/0.000
# so they land as raw 1/0 at quantres 3.
mnd::quantmax = 2147483;
mnd::quantmin = -2147483;
mnd::quantres = 3;

device::worker {
    host = env("S1_WORKER_HOST");   # the XLM-R worker's address, from the environment like the login
    port = 4780;
    user = env("XLM_USER");
    pass = env("XLM_PASS");
}

in::q = embed("worker", "work/q/text.txt", "work/sentencepiece.bpe.model");
in::labs = csv("work/labels_u.csv");        # [D,256] unit rows at 10^-3
in::cand = csv("work/q/cand_d.csv");        # [1,D] raw 1/0: candidate description rows
in::d2l = csv("work/q/d2l.csv");            # [D,32] raw 1/0: row i belongs to label column j
in::req = csv("work/q/req.csv");            # [4,32] row 0 candidate columns, row 2 the risk in column 0
in::ppolicy = csv("proto_policy.csv");      # [4,4] per risk: t_auto, t_verify (cosine margin, permille), warm, min_n
in::sum = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "sum");    # [32,256]
in::n = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "n");        # [1,32]
in::mean = dqt("work/xlm-stats.dqt", "mean");      # [1,1024]
in::w = dqt("work/xlm-stats.dqt", "whiten");       # [256,1024]
in::r32 = csv("work/ranges/r32.csv");       # [1,32] 0..31
in::r4 = csv("work/ranges/r4.csv");         # [1,4]
in::ok = 256 1 ones;
in::rk = 1 256 ones;

# pick(row [1,N], rn [1,N] = 0..N-1, idx [1,1]) -> the one-hot at idx, and row's value there
calc::lambda_flow pick(row, rn, idx) {
    rn 0 scalar_mul 1 add o =
    o idx scalar_mul irow =
    rn irow == h =
    h transpose hc =
    row hc matmul v =
} return h, v;

calc::lambda_flow classify(q, labs, cand, d2l, req, ppolicy, sum, n, mean, w, r32, r4, ok, rk) {
    # --- the text's unit vector, as 02_xlm_classify.mnd
    q mean sub c =
    c w transpose matmul 100 div z3 =
    z3 z3 mul ok matmul isqrt nq =
    z3 1000 scalar_mul nq rk matmul div u =

    # --- the anchor verdict (the speed edition's zero-shot lane)
    u labs transpose matmul s =               # [1,D] cosine x 10^6
    cand 1 sub cm =
    cm 10000000 scalar_mul pen =
    s cand mul pen add sm =
    sm argmax best =

    # --- the request: candidate columns and the policy row of its risk
    req 1000 div rq =
    r4 transpose r4c =
    r4c 0 == e0 =
    r4c 1 == e1 =
    r4c 2 == e2 =
    r4c 3 == e3 =
    e0 transpose e0r =
    e2 transpose e2r =
    e0r rq matmul cmask =                     # [1,32] candidates
    e2r rq matmul riskrow =
    r32 transpose r32c =
    r32c 0 == f0 =
    riskrow f0 matmul ridx =                  # [1,1] 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high
    r4 0 scalar_mul 1 add o4 =
    ridx o4 matmul rrow =
    r4 rrow == rsel =
    rsel ppolicy matmul thr =                 # [1,4] the policy row
    thr e0 matmul t_auto =
    thr e1 matmul t_verify =
    thr e2 matmul warm =                      # [1,1] how many texts the anchor is worth
    thr e3 matmul min_n =                     # [1,1] texts a label needs before the judge answers alone

    # --- one anchor per label: the unit mean of its description rows
    d2l transpose labs matmul A =             # [32,256] the sum of L's description rows
    A A mul ok matmul isqrt na =              # [32,1]
    A 1000 scalar_mul na rk matmul div a =    # unit rows (0 where L has no description)

    # --- the centroids: mean of (warm copies of the anchor + the recorded vectors), normalised
    r32 0 scalar_mul 1 add o32 =
    o32 transpose o32c =                      # [32,1]
    o32c warm matmul wcol =                   # [32,1] warm on every row
    wcol rk matmul W =                        # [32,256]
    a W mul aw =                              # warm * a_L
    aw sum add c0 =
    n transpose nc =                          # [32,1]
    nc wcol add nn =                          # n_L + warm
    nn rk matmul NN =
    c0 NN div c1 =                            # the mean: components <= 1000
    c1 c1 mul ok matmul isqrt ncn =
    c1 1000 scalar_mul ncn rk matmul div cen = # unit centroid rows (0 where nothing is known)

    # --- the prototype verdict over the candidates
    u cen transpose matmul ps0 =              # [1,32] cosine x 10^6
    cmask 1 sub cmm =
    cmm 10000000 scalar_mul penl =
    ps0 cmask mul penl add ps =               # non-candidates at -10^7
    ps argmax pbest =
    ps r32 pbest pick hb, p1 =
    hb 1000000 scalar_mul knock =
    ps knock sub pk =
    pk argmax psecond =
    ps r32 psecond pick hb2, p2 =
    p1 p2 sub pmargin =                       # x 10^6
    n r32 pbest pick hn, nbest =              # how many recorded texts back the verdict
    t_auto 1000 scalar_mul ta =               # permille of cosine -> x 10^6
    t_verify 1000 scalar_mul tv =
    pmargin ta >= ga0 =
    nbest min_n >= enough =                   # the judge has seen enough of the winning label
    ga0 enough mul ga =
    pmargin tv >= gv =
    ga gv add ptier =
} return best, s, pbest, pmargin, ptier, nbest, ps, u;

out::s = csv("work/q/xlm_scores.csv");
out::ps = csv("work/q/proto_scores.csv");
out::u = csv("work/q/u.csv");
```

Read it as four blocks. The first is the first tutorial's classifier
unchanged: the text's unit vector `u`, its cosine to every description row
(`s`), the masked `argmax` (`best`). The second picks the policy row of the
request's risk, the lookup's idiom. The third builds the 32 centroids: the
per-label anchor from the `d2l` one-hot, then
`unit((warm·a + sum) / (warm + n))`. The mean is taken *before* the norm on
purpose: `isqrt` squares its input, and a sum of fifty unit vectors would
already overflow int32 there; a mean never does. The fourth block scores
`u` against the centroids, masks the non-candidates to −10⁷, and reads off
the best, the margin to the runner-up (× 10⁶, the lane's unit) and
`nbest`, how many texts back the verdict.

The tier is the margin against the policy row, with one more condition:
`nbest >= min_n`. An anchor-only verdict is zero-shot, not memory; the
judge may answer alone only once it has learned `min_n` texts (10) of the
label it is choosing. Until then every unseen text goes on to the teacher
of part 1 and, if the rule of part 3 holds, is learned — which is how the
judge earns the right to answer.

`proto_policy.csv`, per risk level (`t_auto`, `t_verify` in permille of
cosine margin, `warm`, `min_n`):

```text
0.050,0.030,0.003,0.010
0.080,0.030,0.003,0.010
0.150,0.030,0.003,0.020
0.080,0.030,0.003,0.010
```

The thresholds come from the benchmark of part 4: at 80 ‰ (medium risk)
the judge answers between a quarter and a half of unseen texts, depending
on the learn rule, at the teacher's accuracy; 50 ‰ trades accuracy for
coverage, 150 ‰ the other way.

`u` is also written to `work/q/u.csv`: the record of part 3 reads it from
there, so learning a text never calls the worker twice.

### 3. Both memories learn

`03_record_proto.mnd` is the outer product again, on the other memory:
`sum += yᵀ · u`, `n += y`. A row of 256 zeros stands for a text recorded
without a vector (a hand record, an older dataset line): it adds nothing
and does not count.

```mnd
# 03_record_proto.mnd -- put one text's vector into the centroid memory
#
#   (04_query.sh's record_both does this right after 03_record.mnd)
#
# The text's whitened unit vector u [1,256] was written to work/q/u.csv by
# 02_proto_classify.mnd when the text was classified, so recording needs no
# second worker call. The update is one outer product:
#
#   sum[L, :] += u      n[L] += 1      for the label's column L (work/q/label.csv)
#
# A row of 256 zeros stands for "recorded without a vector" (a hand record,
# an older dataset line): it adds nothing and does not count, so the
# centroid stays the mean of real vectors. Written in place, like 03_record.mnd.
mnd::quantmax = 2147483;
mnd::quantmin = -2147483;
mnd::quantres = 3;

in::lab = csv("work/q/label.csv");          # [1,1] the label's column
in::u = csv("work/q/u.csv");                # [1,256] unit vector at 10^-3
in::sum = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "sum");    # [32,256]
in::n = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "n");        # [1,32]
in::r32 = csv("work/ranges/r32.csv");       # [1,32] 0..31
in::ok = 256 1 ones;

calc::lambda_flow outer_eq(u, v) {
    u 0 scalar_mul 1 add uo =
    v 0 scalar_mul 1 add vo =
    u vo matmul lhs =
    uo v matmul rhs =
    lhs rhs == m =
} return m;

calc::lambda_flow record(lab, u, sum, n, r32, ok) {
    lab 1000 div lidx =
    lidx r32 outer_eq y =                     # [1,32] one-hot of the label
    u u mul ok matmul nz0 =                   # [1,1] |u|^2, 0 for the all-zero row
    nz0 0 > nz =                              # [1,1] 1 when there is a vector
    y transpose yc =
    yc nz matmul yvc =                        # [32,1] the one-hot, or zeros
    yvc u matmul d =                          # [32,256] the vector under its label
    sum d add sum_new =
    yvc transpose yv =
    n yv add n_new =
} return sum_new, n_new;

out::sum_new = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "sum");
out::n_new = dqt("work/protos.dqt", "n");
```

The shell's `record_both` runs `03_record.mnd`, then this, and appends
`label<TAB>text` to `work/memory.tsv` and the 256 numbers of `u` to the
same line of `work/vectors.csv`. Two files, row-aligned, are the whole
dataset; part 4 replays them.

## 3. The loop, and what it learns

*Known text answers from the cache; the prototype judge answers when it
has earned it; the entailment worker decides the rest, and only what both
lanes agree on is written to the memories. The rest waits for you.*

### 1. The loop

`04_query.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# ============================================================================
# 04_query.sh -- the loop, accuracy edition: the cache; the prototype judge; the entailment teacher; learn what both agree on
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# usage: ./04_query.sh [--risk low|medium|high] "Bitte bis Freitag den Vertrag prüfen" urgent later careful
#        ./04_query.sh "text" spam="unsolicited advertising or a scam" ham="a normal message"
#        ./04_query.sh --yesno "Please wire the deposit today." "This message asks for money to be sent" ["its negation"]
#        ./04_query.sh --score "The kitchen will be repainted next spring." 1="no action" 2="look this week" 3="act today"
#        S1_NO_RECORD=1 ./04_query.sh ...      ask, do not learn
#        S1_LEARN=250 ./04_query.sh ...        min NLI margin (permille of P(entail)) to learn
#        S1_LEARN_RULE=agree|nli|all           what is learned: `agree` (default) the NLI label when the XLM-R
#                                              zero-shot verdict (the anchor) AGREES and the margin clears S1_LEARN;
#                                              `nli` the NLI label above S1_LEARN alone; `all` every NLI label
#        S1_XLM=always ./04_query.sh ...       TRAINING MODE: both lanes run on every request (the answer
#                                              does not change); the learn rule still applies. 05_eval.sh measures in it
#        S1_SELF_LEARN=1 ./04_query.sh ...     also learn an answer the prototype judge gave alone (off: the
#                                              judge never teaches itself)
#
# needs: both memories (./00_setup.sh), both workers (. ~/.config/maned/xlm.env; . ~/.config/maned/nli.env)
# does:  one request, in order:
#          1. 01_lookup.mnd         the count memory: KNOWN text? Then its label answers in ~8 ms
#             (the count judge's tier is reported but no longer decides: it does not generalise)
#          2. 02_proto_classify.mnd one XLM-R embedding on the worker; the prototype judge scores it
#             against the learned centroids (warm-started with the label anchors). Cosine margin
#             >= t_auto AND at least min_n texts learned under the winning label (proto_policy.csv,
#             per risk): the judge answers, "proto:auto"; until then every unseen text is taught
#          3. otherwise the entailment worker (nli/nli_lane.py + 02_nli_classify.mnd) tests every
#             candidate hypothesis: the most entailed one answers, "nli"
#          4. learn: whenever the NLI ran, its label goes into BOTH memories (03_record.mnd,
#             03_record_proto.mnd) when the rule holds - by default when the XLM-R zero-shot verdict
#             (the anchor the judge was computed alongside) agrees with it and its margin clears
#             S1_LEARN. Gating on the judge's OWN verdict instead was measured to feed it its own
#             answers: 63 % label precision and a judge that stops growing. Otherwise the answer is held in
#             work/pending.tsv with both verdicts and the text's vector (resolve later: decide.py --resolve)
#        One line per request goes to work/decisions.tsv.
# A yes/no question is the labels `yes` (the statement) and `no` (its
# negation, given or generated); a Score question's label names are the ranks.
# The function `decide` is the whole of it; 05_eval.sh sources this file with
# S1_LIB=1 to reuse it.
# ============================================================================
. "$(dirname "$0")/_common.sh"

# decide RISK NAME[=DESCRIPTION]...   (the text is in work/q/text.txt; ordinal=1 when the names are ranks)
# -> answer via how t_answer, the lookup's values, anchor_* proto_* nli_* when they ran, and for the
#    trace: xlm_name xlm_col xlm_cos xlm_margin t_xlm p_xlm = the teacher (the NLI when it ran), recorded held
decide() {
  risk=$1; shift
  names=""; reqargs=""
  for a in "$@"; do
    n=${a%%=*}; names="$names $n"
    if [ "${ordinal:-0}" = 1 ]; then reqargs="$reqargs $n=$n"; else reqargs="$reqargs $n"; fi
  done
  lookup "$risk" $reqargs
  best_name=$(name_of "$best"); kbest_name=$(name_of "$kbest")
  answer=""; via=""; how=""; recorded=""; held=""; disputed=0
  anchor_name=""; proto_name=""; proto_margin=""; proto_tier=""; proto_n=""; nli_name=""; nli_margin=""; agree=""
  xlm_name=""; xlm_col=""; xlm_cos=""; xlm_margin=""; p_xlm=""; t_proto=0; t_nli=0; t_xlm=0
  : > work/q/u.csv
  if [ "$known" = 1 ]; then answer=$kbest_name; via="memory:known"; how=0; fi
  if [ -z "$answer" ] || [ "${S1_XLM:-}" = always ]; then
    for a in "$@"; do describe "$a"; done
    proto $names
    if [ -z "$answer" ] && [ "$proto_tier" = 2 ]; then answer=$proto_name; via="proto:auto"; how=4; fi
    if [ -z "$answer" ] || [ "${S1_XLM:-}" = always ]; then
      nli $names
      [ -z "$answer" ] && { answer=$nli_name; via="nli"; how=3; }
      agree=0; [ "$anchor_name" = "$nli_name" ] && agree=1   # the ANCHOR verdict: fixed, so the gate cannot feed the judge its own answers
      xlm_name=$nli_name; xlm_col=$nli_col; xlm_cos=$nli_p; xlm_margin=$nli_margin
      learn=${S1_LEARN:-250}; confident=0
      case ${S1_LEARN_RULE:-agree} in
        agree) [ "$agree" = 1 ] && [ "$nli_margin" -ge "$((learn * 1000))" ] && confident=1 ;;
        nli)   [ "$nli_margin" -ge "$((learn * 1000))" ] && confident=1 ;;
        all)   confident=1 ;;
        *) echo "error: S1_LEARN_RULE must be agree, nli or all" >&2; exit 1 ;;
      esac
      if [ "${S1_NO_RECORD:-}" != 1 ]; then
        if [ "$known" = 1 ] && [ "$nli_name" = "$kbest_name" ]; then :
        elif [ "$confident" = 1 ]; then record_both "$nli_name"; recorded=$nli_name
        else held=$((nli_margin / 1000))
          printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$nli_name" "$held" "$proto_name" "$(echo $names | tr ' ' '|')" "$(cat work/q/text.txt)" "$(cat work/q/u.csv)" >> work/pending.tsv; fi
      fi
    elif [ "${S1_SELF_LEARN:-0}" = 1 ] && [ "${S1_NO_RECORD:-}" != 1 ]; then
      record_both "$proto_name"; recorded=$proto_name
    fi
    [ -n "$xlm_name" ] || { xlm_name=$anchor_name; xlm_col=$anchor_col; xlm_cos=$anchor_cos; xlm_margin=$anchor_margin; }
    p_xlm=$(nth "$p" "$xlm_col")
  fi
  t_xlm=$((t_proto + t_nli))
  t_answer=$t_lookup
  case $how in 4) t_answer=$((t_lookup + t_proto)) ;; 3) t_answer=$((t_lookup + t_proto + t_nli)) ;; esac
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(date +%FT%T)" "$answer" "$via" "$t_answer" "$tier" "$p_best" "${xlm_name:--}" \
    "${recorded:+recorded:$recorded}" "$(cat work/q/text.txt)" >> work/decisions.tsv
}

# report -> the transcript of the last decide
report() {
  printf 'memory  %-10s p %s%%o  tier %s (%s)  known %s' "$best_name" "$p_best" "$tier" "$(tiername "$tier")" "$known"
  [ "$known" = 1 ] && printf ' (%s, coverage %s/%s)' "$kbest_name" "$cov_best" "$q"
  printf '   %s ms\n' "$t_lookup"
  [ -n "$proto_name" ] && printf 'proto   %-10s cos %s  margin %s%%o  tier %s (%s)  from %s texts   anchor %s (cos %s)   %s ms\n' \
    "$proto_name" "$proto_cos" "$((proto_margin / 1000))" "$proto_tier" "$(tiername "$proto_tier")" "$proto_n" "$anchor_name" "$anchor_cos" "$t_proto"
  [ -n "$nli_name" ] && printf 'nli     %-10s P(entail) %s  margin %s%%o   %s   %s ms\n' \
    "$nli_name" "$nli_p" "$((nli_margin / 1000))" "$([ "$agree" = 1 ] && echo AGREE || echo DISAGREE)" "$t_nli"
  printf 'ANSWER  %-10s via %s in %s ms' "$answer" "$via" "$t_answer"
  [ -n "$recorded" ] && printf '  (recorded as %s)' "$recorded"
  [ -n "$held" ] && printf '  HELD: %s (NLI margin %s%%o) -> work/pending.tsv, not learned' \
    "$([ "$agree" = 1 ] && echo 'low teacher confidence' || echo 'the two lanes disagree')" "$held"
  printf '\n'
}

if [ "${S1_LIB:-}" != 1 ]; then
  need work/memory.dqt "./00_setup.sh"
  need work/protos.dqt "./00_setup.sh"
  risk=1; kind=choice
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case $1 in
      --risk) case ${2:-} in low) risk=0 ;; medium) risk=1 ;; high) risk=2 ;; *) echo "usage: --risk low|medium|high" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; shift 2 ;;
      --yesno) kind=yesno; shift ;;
      --score) kind=score; shift ;;
      *) break ;;
    esac
  done
  [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: $0 [--risk low|medium|high] [--yesno | --score] \"text\" label[=description]..." >&2; exit 1; }
  text=$1; shift
  prep "$text"
  case $kind in
    choice)
      decide "$risk" "$@"; report ;;
    yesno)
      statement=$1
      negation=${2:-"It is not the case that $(printf '%s' "$statement" | cut -c1 | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')$(printf '%s' "$statement" | cut -c2-)"}
      decide "$risk" "yes=$statement" "no=$negation"; report
      printf 'P(yes)  %s%%o\n' "$(nth "$p" "$(col_of yes)")" ;;
    score)
      for a in "$@"; do case ${a%%=*} in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "error: a Score question's label names are the ranks: 1=\"...\" 2=\"...\"" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; done
      ordinal=1 decide "$risk" "$@"; report
      printf 'expected rank %s\n' "$(echo "$expected" | awk '{printf "%.2f", $1 / 1000}')" ;;
  esac
fi
```

`decide` is five moves. The lookup, and a KNOWN text answers at once. The
prototype judge, and a confident one with enough evidence answers,
`proto:auto`. Otherwise the NLI lane, `nli`. Then the learning rule, and
one line to `work/decisions.tsv`. The count judge's tier and probability
are still reported in the first line of the transcript — they are what the
first tutorial's loop would have done — but they no longer decide.

The first text through an empty loop:

```sh
. ~/.config/maned/xlm.env; . ~/.config/maned/nli.env
./04_query.sh "Our servers crashed again, customers cannot log in, fix it within the hour." urgent later careful
```

```text
memory  urgent     p 333%o  tier 0 (review)  known 0   73 ms
proto   urgent     cos 0.535  margin 176%o  tier 1 (verify)  from 0 texts   anchor urgent (cos 0.661)   1862 ms
nli     urgent     P(entail) 0.519  margin 200%o   AGREE   6100 ms
ANSWER  urgent     via nli in 8035 ms  HELD: low teacher confidence (NLI margin 200%o) -> work/pending.tsv, not learned
```

Four lines now. The judge's verdict comes with its cosine, margin, tier,
how many texts back it and which anchor the speed edition would have
picked; the teacher's with its P(entail), margin and whether the two
lanes agree; and the answer with what happened to it.

The seconds on the `nli` line are honest and not the worker's fault: the
outputs on this page were captured against the NLI kernel running under
QEMU's software emulation on the laptop that wrote them. On the bare-metal
worker the same three-hypothesis call takes about 0.7 s, and the
`proto` line's 300 ms is the real XLM worker over the LAN.

### 2. The rule

The teacher's label is written to both memories when `S1_LEARN_RULE`
holds. The default, **agree**, needs two things: the XLM's zero-shot
verdict — the anchor, the label whose description the text is nearest to —
named the same label as the teacher, and the NLI margin — P(entail) of the
winner minus the runner-up's — clears `S1_LEARN`, 250 ‰. On the benchmark
of part 4 this writes a quarter of the texts at 76 % label precision, where
either teacher alone would write them all at 44–54 %. A loop that learns a
wrong label pays for it on every later text; a loop that holds a doubtful
one pays a line in a file.

Why the anchor and not the judge itself? We measured that too: a gate that
asks the prototype judge to agree writes only the texts the judge already
believes, so the centroids confirm themselves — 63 % label precision and a
judge that stops growing at 0.37. The anchor is fixed, so the gate cannot
feed the judge its own answers.

Everything held goes to `work/pending.tsv` with both verdicts and the
text's vector, so that confirming it later costs no worker call:

```sh
./04_query.sh "Here is the monthly newsletter with photos from the picnic." urgent later careful
cut -f1-5 work/pending.tsv
```

```text
memory  urgent     p 333%o  tier 0 (review)  known 0   74 ms
proto   later      cos 0.434  margin 184%o  tier 1 (verify)  from 0 texts   anchor later (cos 0.426)   473 ms
nli     urgent     P(entail) 0.694  margin 520%o   DISAGREE   4953 ms
ANSWER  urgent     via nli in 5500 ms  HELD: the two lanes disagree (NLI margin 520%o) -> work/pending.tsv, not learned
```

```text
urgent	200	urgent	urgent|later|careful	Our servers crashed again, customers cannot log in, fix it within the hour.
urgent	520	later	urgent|later|careful	Here is the monthly newsletter with photos from the picnic.
```

`S1_LEARN_RULE=nli` learns every teacher label above the margin, faster
and noisier; `all` learns everything, the speed edition's training mode.
The judge never learns its own `proto:auto` answers unless you say so
(`S1_SELF_LEARN=1`): a judge that teaches itself drifts.

### 3. A known text

Teach the loop a text — here with the rule relaxed, to see the write —
and ask again:

```sh
S1_LEARN_RULE=all ./04_query.sh "Please review the attached contract clauses on liability before signing." urgent later careful
./04_query.sh "Please review the attached contract clauses on liability before signing." urgent later careful
```

```text
memory  urgent     p 333%o  tier 0 (review)  known 0   99 ms
proto   careful    cos 0.664  margin 376%o  tier 1 (verify)  from 0 texts   anchor careful (cos 0.700)   1028 ms
nli     careful    P(entail) 0.979  margin 962%o   AGREE   5238 ms
ANSWER  careful    via nli in 6365 ms  (recorded as careful)

memory  careful    p 1000%o  tier 2 (auto)  known 1 (careful, coverage 29/29)   70 ms
ANSWER  careful    via memory:known in 70 ms
```

The second time the count memory recognises it and answers in a few
milliseconds; neither worker is called. That lane is the whole of the
speed edition's advantage, and this edition keeps it.

## 4. Measure it

*The same corpus and the same four passes as the first tutorial, through
this loop; then the benchmark on nine public datasets that the thresholds
and the claims of this page come from; then the rebuild of both memories.*

### 1. The corpus, four passes

`05_eval.sh` is the first tutorial's, run against this `decide`: the
memories are emptied, the 108 messages go through cold, then warm, then
the 36 variants and the 36 unseen, in training mode — both lanes run on
every request so every row carries the teacher's label — and the learning
rule still decides what is written. The rows are the same 15 integers, so
`05_eval.mnd` is shared unchanged; the only translation is that an answer
by the prototype judge alone is written as the first tutorial's "judge
auto", and the teacher column holds the NLI label.

```sh
. ~/.config/maned/xlm.env; . ~/.config/maned/nli.env
./05_eval.sh
```

```text
== pass 0 cold: 108 requests ==
== pass 1 warm: 108 requests ==
== pass 2 variants: 36 requests ==
== pass 3 unseen: 36 requests ==
288 requests in 2239 s -> work/eval/rows.csv
```

```text
== 05_eval.mnd over work/eval/rows.csv (columns: cold, warm, variants, unseen) ==
xlm_acc : [1x4] = [694, 694, 666, 750]
ans_acc : [1x4] = [694, 768, 777, 750]
n_known : [1x4] = [0, 47, 17, 0]
n_judge : [1x4] = [33, 21, 8, 17]
n_xlm : [1x4] = [75, 40, 11, 19]
judge_auto_acc : [1x4] = [0, 872, 764, 0]
n_judge_auto : [1x4] = [0, 47, 17, 0]
checks : [1x4] = [1, 0, 1, 1]
t_answer : [1x4] = [5169, 2733, 2513, 4524]
t_xlm : [1x4] = [7069, 6999, 7537, 8094]
t_lookup : [1x4] = [76, 77, 83, 83]
xlm_acc_lang4 : [1x4] = [777, 638, 666, 0]
warm pass: 47 of the 47 texts learned in the cold pass were answered from memory
checks: cold-never-known, learned-texts-known-warm, warm-as-right-as-teacher, unseen-auto->=teacher = 1 1 1 1 (1 = PASS)
learned 47 of 180 texts; 87% of the learned labels are right (S1_LEARN_RULE=agree, S1_LEARN=250)
```

The last line is this edition's own number: of the texts the loop was
allowed to write under the `agree` rule, how many carried the right label.

### 2. The benchmark

Nine public datasets (AG News, Emotion, TweetEval offensive and sentiment,
SMS Spam, SST-2, SST-5, Yelp, DBpedia; three question shapes), 240 texts
learned per dataset and 33 unseen texts each, every configuration on the
same texts. The harness is `work/eval_suite/` of the speed edition; its
README describes the protocol, the trace format and the three studies.
Headline numbers on the 264 unseen texts of the eight datasets whose NLI
replies the study had cached:

| configuration (240 texts learned per dataset) | judge on unseen text | final answer | answered without the second worker |
|---|---|---|---|
| speed-first: count judge, XLM-R teacher | 0.39 | 0.45 | — (one worker) |
| NLI teacher alone, no judge | — | 0.48 | 0 % |
| accuracy-first, `S1_LEARN_RULE=agree`: prototype judge, NLI teacher | 0.44 | 0.48 (medium risk; 0.48 with the threshold chosen on the other datasets) | 48 % |
| accuracy-first, `S1_LEARN_RULE=nli`: prototype judge, NLI teacher | 0.44 | 0.52 (medium risk; 0.48 with the threshold chosen on the other datasets) | 26 % |

The prototype judge by texts learned (40 → 80 → 160 → 240): `agree`: 0.42 → 0.40 → 0.42 → 0.44; `nli`: 0.39 → 0.41 → 0.45 → 0.44. The count judge of the speed edition on the same texts: 0.35 → 0.38 → 0.39 → 0.40.

What `agree` wrote while learning 1920 texts: 479 (25 %) at 75 % label precision; 1441 held at 47 %; the two lanes agreed on 38 % of texts.

What `nli` wrote while learning 1920 texts: 1023 (53 %) at 64 % label precision; 897 held at 43 %; the two lanes agreed on 38 % of texts.

Read the table as the trade this page is about. The prototype judge is the
only judge that grows with volume; the count judge of the speed edition
sits at 0.39 whatever it learns. The agreement rule writes a quarter of
the texts at 75 % label precision and answers half of the unseen texts
itself at the teacher's accuracy; the plain `nli` rule writes twice as
many labels at 64 % precision, grows the judge faster and ends two to four
points above the teacher alone while answering a quarter of the texts
itself. On a corpus of this size the second is the better bet for accuracy
and the first for a memory you can trust line by line, and the knob is
yours. The gold row of the offline study — 0.59 with true labels — says
where the remaining headroom is: in the teachers, not the judge.

### 3. Rebuild both memories

`06_rebuild.sh` empties both memories and replays `work/memory.tsv`
together with `work/vectors.csv`, line by line, through the two record
programs, then compares the bytes:

```sh
./06_rebuild.sh
```

```text
replayed 1 texts in 0 s
work/memory.dqt is byte-identical to the one it replaced: the incremental records equal a from-scratch computation
work/protos.dqt is byte-identical to the one it replaced: the incremental records equal a from-scratch computation
```

Integer sums are exact and order-free, so byte identity is the expected
result, not a lucky one. Fix a label in the text file — and drop or keep
its vector line with it — and the memories follow.

## 5. The app

*The lookup in-process through the binding as before; the judge, the
teacher and the two records as the processes they are; the same command
line, plus a review queue that feeds the centroid memory.*

### 1. One Python file

`consumers/python/decide.py` is the first tutorial's app with the three
new moves. `proto()` writes the two masks and runs `02_proto_classify.mnd`;
`nli()` runs `nli/nli_lane.py` and `02_nli_classify.mnd`; `record_both()`
runs the two record programs and appends the two dataset lines, then
reloads the lookup. `decide()` is the shell's `decide`, line for line, and
returns the typed decision with both lanes' verdicts in it.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""A Python app that IS a System One, accuracy edition: the known-text lookup
runs in-process through the manedpy binding; the prototype judge, the
entailment teacher and the two records are maned-run processes.

    pip install manedpy sentencepiece                     # manedpy 0.4.2 or newer
    python3 consumers/python/decide.py                    # the three demo questions
    python3 consumers/python/decide.py [--risk low|medium|high] [--train] "text" label[=description]...
    python3 consumers/python/decide.py --yesno "text" "statement" ["negation"]
    python3 consumers/python/decide.py --score "text" 1="..." 2="..." 3="..."
    python3 consumers/python/decide.py --pending          # answers held for review
    python3 consumers/python/decide.py --resolve [accept] # confirm them, then learn

What `decide` does per question, in order:
  1. lookup   01_lookup.mnd through manedpy: a KNOWN text answers from the count memory in ~8 ms
  2. proto    else maned-run 02_proto_classify.mnd: one XLM-R embedding, scored against the
              learned centroids (protos.dqt). Margin >= t_auto with >= min_n texts learned
              under the winning label (proto_policy.csv): the judge answers, "proto:auto"
  3. nli      else nli/nli_lane.py asks the entailment worker about every candidate
              hypothesis and 02_nli_classify.mnd picks the most entailed: "nli"
  4. learn    whenever the teacher ran: its label goes into BOTH memories (03_record.mnd,
              03_record_proto.mnd) when the rule holds - by default when the XLM-R zero-shot
              verdict (the anchor) agrees and the NLI margin clears S1_LEARN (250 permille); otherwise the answer
              is held in work/pending.tsv with both verdicts and the text's vector
Training mode (train=True, --train): both lanes run on every request; the learn rule still decides.
Env: S1_LEARN, S1_LEARN_RULE=agree|nli|all, S1_SELF_LEARN=1, MANED_RUN, S1_HYPOTHESES; the
workers' addresses and logins from ~/.config/maned/xlm.env and ~/.config/maned/nli.env.
Strings, files and processes are the app's; every number is a program's.
"""
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from manedpy import maned as mnd

PROJECT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
os.chdir(PROJECT)                      # every path in the .mnd files is relative to the project folder
MANED_RUN = os.environ.get("MANED_RUN", "maned-run")
PYTHON = os.environ.get("S1_PYTHON", sys.executable)
TIERS = ["review", "verify", "auto"]
RISK = {"low": 0, "medium": 1, "high": 2}
DEFAULT_LEARN = 250                    # min NLI margin (permille of P(entail)) to learn; measured: 75% of learned labels right at 250 under `agree`
ZERO_VEC = ",".join(["0.000"] * 256)


def load_env():
    """the XLM-R worker's address and login from ~/.config/maned/xlm.env, unless already in the
    environment (the device blocks read them with env()); nli/nli_lane.py reads nli.env itself"""
    path = os.path.expanduser("~/.config/maned/xlm.env")
    if os.path.exists(path):
        for line in open(path):
            m = re.match(r"\s*(?:export\s+)?(\w+)=(.*)", line)
            if m:
                os.environ.setdefault(m.group(1), m.group(2).strip().strip('"'))


def run_mnd(name):
    """maned-run PROGRAM -> {output: [raw ints]} from the lines 'name : [shape] = [values]'"""
    r = subprocess.run([MANED_RUN, name], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit("%s failed:\n%s%s" % (name, r.stdout, r.stderr))
    return {m.group(1): [int(v) for v in m.group(2).split(",")]
            for m in re.finditer(r"^(\w+) : \[[^\]]*\] = \[([^\]]*)\]", r.stdout, re.M)}


def lines(path):
    return [l.rstrip("\n") for l in open(path, encoding="utf-8")] if os.path.exists(path) else []


def col_of(name):
    """work/labels.tsv: line i is column i of both memories; a new name takes the next column"""
    names = lines("work/labels.tsv")
    if name not in names:
        names.append(name)
        open("work/labels.tsv", "a", encoding="utf-8").write(name + "\n")
    return names.index(name)


def hypothesis_of(name, desc):
    """the sentence the NLI worker tests the text against: $S1_HYPOTHESES, else corpus/hypotheses.tsv, else the description"""
    for path in (os.environ.get("S1_HYPOTHESES", ""), "corpus/hypotheses.tsv"):
        for l in lines(path) if path else []:
            n, _, h = l.partition("\t")
            if n == name and h:
                return h
    return desc


def describe(name, desc):
    """each (label, description) is embedded once on the worker: work/descs.tsv row i = work/labels_u.csv row i;
    the label's hypothesis goes to work/descs_nli.tsv (nothing embedded)"""
    hyp = "%s\t%s" % (name, hypothesis_of(name, desc))
    if hyp not in lines("work/descs_nli.tsv"):
        open("work/descs_nli.tsv", "a", encoding="utf-8").write(hyp + "\n")
    if "%s\t%s" % (name, desc) in lines("work/descs.tsv"):
        return
    open("work/q/new_descs.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(desc + "\n")
    run_mnd("02_label_embed.mnd")
    open("work/labels_u.csv", "a").write(open("work/q/new_u.csv").read())
    open("work/descs.tsv", "a", encoding="utf-8").write("%s\t%s\n" % (name, desc))


def req_csv(names, risk, ordinal):
    """the [4,32] request: candidate columns, their ranks, the risk level"""
    cand, ordv = [0] * 32, [0] * 32
    for n in names:
        cand[col_of(n)] = 1
        ordv[col_of(n)] = ordinal.get(n, 0)
    rows = [cand, ordv, [risk] + [0] * 31, [0] * 32]
    return "".join(",".join(str(v) for v in r) + "\n" for r in rows)


def values(part):
    """an out:: csv part, decoded at quantres 3 ('0.955'), back to raw ints (955)"""
    return [int(round(float(x) * 1000)) for x in part.decode().strip().split(",")]


def mask_csv(registry, names):
    """work/q/cand_d.csv: 1 for the registry rows of the candidates (written 0.001 -> raw 1 at quantres 3)"""
    rows = [l.split("\t", 1)[0] for l in lines(registry)]
    open("work/q/cand_d.csv", "w").write(",".join("0.001" if r in names else "0.000" for r in rows) + "\n")
    return rows


def label_margin(rows, names, s):
    """top1 - top2 (x10^6) over the candidate LABELS, each scored by the max over its registry rows"""
    bylabel = {}
    for i, dn in enumerate(rows):
        if dn in names and i < len(s):
            bylabel[dn] = max(bylabel.get(dn, -10 ** 9), s[i])
    top = sorted(bylabel.values(), reverse=True)
    return (top[0] - top[1]) if len(top) >= 2 else 10 ** 9


# the lookup opens work/q/text.txt and work/q/req.csv when it loads; decide() rewrites them on
# every call, so a fresh checkout only needs the two placeholders to exist
os.makedirs("work/q/out", exist_ok=True)
for _f, _blank in (("work/q/text.txt", "\n"), ("work/q/req.csv", ("0," * 31 + "0\n") * 4)):
    if not os.path.exists(_f):
        open(_f, "w").write(_blank)
lookup = mnd.load("01_lookup.mnd")


def proto(names):
    """02_proto_classify.mnd: the anchor verdict and the prototype judge from ONE embedding; u lands in work/q/u.csv"""
    descs = mask_csv("work/descs.tsv", names)
    open("work/q/d2l.csv", "w").write("".join(
        ",".join("0.001" if j == col_of(dn) else "0.000" for j in range(32)) + "\n" for dn in descs))
    t = time.time()
    out = run_mnd("02_proto_classify.mnd")
    label = lines("work/labels.tsv")
    arow = out["best"][0]
    pcol = out["pbest"][0]
    return {"anchor": label[col_of(descs[arow])], "anchor_cos": out["s"][arow] / 1e6, "anchor_margin": label_margin(descs, names, out["s"]),
            "name": label[pcol], "col": pcol, "cos": out["ps"][pcol] / 1e6, "margin": out["pmargin"][0],
            "tier": out["ptier"][0], "n": out["nbest"][0], "ms": int((time.time() - t) * 1000)}


def nli(names):
    """nli/nli_lane.py on every candidate hypothesis, then 02_nli_classify.mnd: the most entailed label"""
    rows = mask_csv("work/descs_nli.tsv", names)
    m = open("work/q/cand_d.csv").read().strip().split(",")
    open("work/q/cand_m.csv", "w").write(",".join("1.000" if float(v) > 0 else "0.000" for v in m) + "\n")
    open("work/q/cand_one.csv", "w").write(",".join("1.000" for _ in m) + "\n")
    t = time.time()
    r = subprocess.run([PYTHON, "nli/nli_lane.py"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit("the NLI worker call failed:\n%s%s" % (r.stdout, r.stderr))
    out = run_mnd("02_nli_classify.mnd")
    row = out["best"][0]
    label = lines("work/labels.tsv")
    return {"name": label[col_of(rows[row])], "col": col_of(rows[row]), "p": out["s"][row] / 1e6,
            "margin": label_margin(rows, names, out["s"]), "ms": int((time.time() - t) * 1000)}


def record_both(name, vec=None):
    """both memories learn (text in work/q/text.txt, NAME): 03_record.mnd and 03_record_proto.mnd rewrite their
    .dqt files; one line goes to work/memory.tsv and its vector (or 256 zeros) to work/vectors.csv"""
    global lookup
    if vec is not None:
        open("work/q/u.csv", "w").write(vec.strip() + "\n")
    elif not os.path.exists("work/q/u.csv") or not open("work/q/u.csv").read().strip():
        open("work/q/u.csv", "w").write(ZERO_VEC + "\n")
    open("work/q/label.csv", "w").write("%d\n" % col_of(name))
    run_mnd("03_record.mnd")
    run_mnd("03_record_proto.mnd")
    open("work/memory.tsv", "a", encoding="utf-8").write("%s\t%s\n" % (name, open("work/q/text.txt", encoding="utf-8").read().rstrip("\n")))
    open("work/vectors.csv", "a").write(open("work/q/u.csv").read().strip() + "\n")
    lookup.close()
    lookup = mnd.load("01_lookup.mnd")      # the memory it loaded has changed on disk


def decide(text, labels, risk="medium", ordinal=None, train=False):
    """labels: {name: description}; ordinal: {name: rank} for Score questions -> the typed decision"""
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    names = list(labels)
    os.makedirs("work/q", exist_ok=True)
    open("work/q/text.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text + "\n")   # for the maned-run lanes
    open("work/q/u.csv", "w").write("")
    t0 = time.time()
    out = lookup.run_files(msg=text.encode(), req=req_csv(names, RISK[risk], ordinal or {}).encode())
    v = {k: values(b) for k, b in out.items()}
    t_lookup = int((time.time() - t0) * 1000)
    best, p_best, tier, known, kbest = v["best"][0], v["p_best"][0], v["tier"][0], v["known"][0], v["kbest"][0]
    p, label = v["p"], lines("work/labels.tsv")
    answer = via = None
    how, pr, nl, agree, recorded, held = 0, None, None, None, None, None
    if known:
        answer, via, how = label[kbest], "memory:known", 0
    if answer is None or train:
        for n, d in labels.items():
            describe(n, d)
        pr = proto(names)
        if answer is None and pr["tier"] == 2:
            answer, via, how = pr["name"], "proto:auto", 4
        if answer is None or train:
            nl = nli(names)
            if answer is None:
                answer, via, how = nl["name"], "nli", 3
            agree = pr["anchor"] == nl["name"]   # the fixed zero-shot verdict, not the judge's own: no feedback loop
            learn = int(os.environ.get("S1_LEARN", DEFAULT_LEARN))
            rule = os.environ.get("S1_LEARN_RULE", "agree")
            confident = {"agree": agree and nl["margin"] >= learn * 1000,
                         "nli": nl["margin"] >= learn * 1000, "all": True}[rule]
            if known and nl["name"] == label[kbest]:
                pass
            elif confident:
                record_both(nl["name"])
                recorded = nl["name"]
            else:
                held = nl["margin"] // 1000
                open("work/pending.tsv", "a", encoding="utf-8").write("%s\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n" % (
                    nl["name"], held, pr["name"], "|".join(names), text, open("work/q/u.csv").read().strip()))
        elif os.environ.get("S1_SELF_LEARN") == "1":
            record_both(pr["name"])
            recorded = pr["name"]
    t_answer = t_lookup + {4: pr["ms"] if pr else 0, 3: (pr["ms"] if pr else 0) + (nl["ms"] if nl else 0)}.get(how, 0)
    return {"answer": answer, "via": via, "tier": TIERS[tier], "known": bool(known),
            "p": {n: p[col_of(n)] for n in names}, "expected": v["expected"][0] / 1000.0,
            "proto": pr, "nli": nl, "agree": agree, "recorded": recorded, "held": held, "ms": t_answer,
            "best": label[best], "p_best": p_best, "coverage": (v["cov_best"][0], v["q"][0]),
            # the row an evaluation keeps: how, best, p_best, tier, known, teacher col, t_answer, t_lookup
            "raw": [how, best, p_best, tier, known, (nl or pr or {}).get("col", -1), t_answer, t_lookup]}


def transcript(d):
    """the decision as the tutorial's lines"""
    out = "memory  %-10s p %d%%o  tier %s  known %d" % (d["best"], d["p_best"], d["tier"], d["known"])
    if d["known"]:
        out += " (coverage %d/%d)" % d["coverage"]
    out += "   %d ms\n" % d["raw"][7]
    pr, nl = d["proto"], d["nli"]
    if pr:
        out += "proto   %-10s cos %.3f  margin %d%%o  tier %s  from %d texts   anchor %s (cos %.3f)   %d ms\n" % (
            pr["name"], pr["cos"], pr["margin"] // 1000, TIERS[pr["tier"]], pr["n"], pr["anchor"], pr["anchor_cos"], pr["ms"])
    if nl:
        out += "nli     %-10s P(entail) %.3f  margin %d%%o   %s   %d ms\n" % (
            nl["name"], nl["p"], nl["margin"] // 1000, "AGREE" if d["agree"] else "DISAGREE", nl["ms"])
    out += "ANSWER  %-10s via %s in %d ms" % (d["answer"], d["via"], d["ms"])
    if d["recorded"]:
        out += "  (recorded as %s)" % d["recorded"]
    if d.get("held") is not None:
        out += "\nHELD    %s (NLI margin %d%%o) -> work/pending.tsv, not learned" % (
            "low teacher confidence" if d["agree"] else "the two lanes disagree", d["held"])
    return out


def show_pending():
    """print the answers held for review (work/pending.tsv): teacher, margin, judge, candidates, text"""
    rows = lines("work/pending.tsv")
    if not rows:
        print("nothing held for review")
        return
    print("teacher\tmargin\tjudge\tcandidates\ttext")
    for r in rows:
        print("\t".join(r.split("\t")[:5]))


def resolve(args):
    """learn the held answers. `--resolve` confirms each one; `--resolve accept` takes the
    teacher's label for every row without asking. A corrected label, or `s` to skip, is read
    from the keyboard; skipped rows stay in the queue. The row's vector feeds the centroid memory."""
    accept_all = bool(args) and args[0] == "accept"
    rows = lines("work/pending.tsv")
    if not rows:
        print("nothing held for review")
        return
    kept = []
    for r in rows:
        f = r.split("\t")
        if len(f) < 5:
            continue
        teacher, margin, judge, cands, text = f[:5]
        vec = f[5] if len(f) > 5 and f[5] else None
        name = teacher
        if not accept_all:
            try:
                ans = input("\n%s\n  candidates: %s\n  teacher: %s (margin %s%%o), judge: %s\n  [Enter]=accept the teacher, a label, or s=skip: "
                            % (text, cands.replace("|", ", "), teacher, margin, judge)).strip()
            except EOFError:
                ans = "s"
            if ans == "s":
                kept.append(r)
                continue
            if ans:
                name = ans
        open("work/q/text.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text + "\n")
        record_both(name, vec or ZERO_VEC)
        print("  learned: %s" % name)
    open("work/pending.tsv", "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(x + "\n" for x in kept))


def main(argv):
    """the command line: a Choice, yes/no or Score question, the review queue, or the demos"""
    load_env()
    if argv and argv[0] == "--pending":
        return show_pending()
    if argv and argv[0] == "--resolve":
        return resolve(argv[1:])
    risk, kind, train = "medium", "choice", False
    while argv and argv[0].startswith("--"):
        flag = argv.pop(0)
        if flag == "--risk":
            risk = argv.pop(0)
        elif flag == "--train":
            train = True
        elif flag in ("--yesno", "--score"):
            kind = flag[2:]
        else:
            sys.exit("unknown flag " + flag)
    if not argv:
        return demo()
    text, args = argv[0], argv[1:]
    if kind == "yesno":
        statement = args[0]
        negation = args[1] if len(args) > 1 else "It is not the case that " + statement[0].lower() + statement[1:]
        d = decide(text, {"yes": statement, "no": negation}, risk, train=train)
        print(transcript(d) + "\nP(yes)  %d%%o" % d["p"]["yes"])
    elif kind == "score":
        labels = dict(a.split("=", 1) for a in args)
        d = decide(text, labels, risk, ordinal={n: int(n) for n in labels}, train=train)
        print(transcript(d) + "\nexpected rank %.2f" % d["expected"])
    else:
        labels = {}
        for a in args:          # name, or name=description; a bare name uses the corpus descriptions, else itself
            name, _, desc = a.partition("=")
            corpus = [l.split("\t", 1)[1] for l in lines("corpus/labels.tsv") if l.startswith(name + "\t")]
            for d in corpus[1:]:
                describe(name, d)
            labels[name] = desc or (corpus[0] if corpus else name)
        print(transcript(decide(text, labels, risk, train=train)))


def demo():
    choice = decide("Our servers crashed again, customers cannot log in, fix it within the hour.",
                    {"urgent": "This message needs action right now: an outage, an emergency, a deadline today.",
                     "later": "This message can wait: an update, a newsletter, something for next week.",
                     "careful": "This message needs care before acting: a contract, a legal clause, a payment detail."})
    print("choice: %s  (via %s, %d ms)" % (choice["answer"], choice["via"], choice["ms"]))

    statement = "This message asks for money to be sent"
    yesno = decide("Please wire the deposit today.",
                   {"yes": statement, "no": "It is not the case that " + statement[0].lower() + statement[1:]})
    print("yes/no: %s  (P(yes) %d‰, via %s, %d ms)" % (yesno["answer"], yesno["p"]["yes"], yesno["via"], yesno["ms"]))

    score = decide("The kitchen will be repainted next spring.",
                   {"1": "no action", "2": "look this week", "3": "act today"}, ordinal={"1": 1, "2": 2, "3": 3})
    print("score:  rank %s, expected %.2f  (via %s, %d ms)" % (score["answer"], score["expected"], score["via"], score["ms"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])
```

```sh
pip install manedpy sentencepiece
python3 consumers/python/decide.py "Bitte bis Freitag den Vertrag prüfen" urgent later careful
python3 consumers/python/decide.py --pending
python3 consumers/python/decide.py --resolve accept
```

```text
memory  urgent     p 333%o  tier review  known 0   73 ms
proto   careful    cos 0.323  margin 208%o  tier verify  from 1 texts   anchor careful (cos 0.296)   200 ms
nli     careful    P(entail) 0.482  margin 106%o   AGREE   4394 ms
ANSWER  careful    via nli in 4667 ms
HELD    low teacher confidence (NLI margin 106%o) -> work/pending.tsv, not learned

$ python3 consumers/python/decide.py --pending
teacher	margin	judge	candidates	text
urgent	200	urgent	urgent|later|careful	Our servers crashed again, customers cannot log in, fix it within the hour.
urgent	520	later	urgent|later|careful	Here is the monthly newsletter with photos from the picnic.
careful	106	careful	urgent|later|careful	Bitte bis Freitag den Vertrag prüfen

$ python3 consumers/python/decide.py --resolve accept
  learned: urgent
  learned: urgent
  learned: careful
```

`--resolve` walks the queue: Enter accepts the teacher's label, a typed
label corrects it, `s` skips. Each confirmed row is recorded into both
memories with the vector it was held with, so the queue is a second
teacher of the judge — you.

### 2. The service, unchanged

`maned-serve 01_lookup.mnd --port 8787` serves the known-text cache
exactly as in the first tutorial, since the program is the same file. The
judge and the teacher are `maned-run` processes by nature (`embed()` is a
source only `maned-run` can load) and a Python process for the NLI client;
an app that wants them resident keeps the Python module loaded, as
`test_ui.py` does.

### 3. Kotlin and Rust

Not in this edition yet. The first tutorial's Kotlin and Rust apps are
complete System Ones of the speed-first kind; the accuracy-first loop
needs an NLI client in each language — a pair tokenizer and one HTTP call —
